source.author: verg
source.text: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_original: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, / et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, / sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro / pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_english: Gods, to whom sovereignty belongs over souls, and silent shades, and Chaos, and Phlegethon, wide realms hushed in night, grant me leave to speak what I have heard; grant me, by your power, to disclose things buried deep in earth and sunk in darkness!

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at frater magnos Lynceus servatur in usus, quem tulit Arene, possit qui rumpere terras et Styga transmisso tacitam deprendere visu.
reuse.text_original: at frater magnos Lynceus servatur in usus, / quem tulit Arene, possit qui rumpere terras / et Styga transmisso tacitam deprendere visu.
reuse.text_english: but their brother Lynceus is preserved for great uses, whom Arene bore, who can split the earth and, with his sight sent across, detect silent Styx.
